methodology.clock: ManualClock — simulated time, identical on every machine

grantResolutionMicros.note: Grant times are sampled by stepping the clock, so they are accurate to the step, rounded up. Figures needing more precision are asked of the limiter directly and labelled "exact".

methodology.note: Behavioural results only. Timing and memory costs are measured separately by bench/perf.mjs on a real clock.

steady-state.title: 1. Steady state — sustained demand past warm-up

idle-recooling.title: 3. Idle → burst — re-cooling after a full warm-up period of idleness
idle-recooling.note: The second burst is throttled like the first: the limiter went fully cold again.

repeated-cycles.title: 4. Repeated burst/idle cycles — drift check over 10 cycles
repeated-cycles.note: Cycle 0 differs: the limiter starts fully cold with an empty timeline.

algorithm-comparison.title: 5. Warm-up vs token bucket vs fixed window vs fixed rate — 300 requests at t=0
algorithm-comparison.note: Not a throughput contest (§13.4). The token bucket and fixed window admit the burst at once by design; the warm-up limiter exists to ramp instead.

warmup-vs-pacing.title: 6. Warm-up vs fixed pacing — pacing smooths, only warm-up ramps
warmup-vs-pacing.note: Fixed pacing holds one interval from the first call to the last. Warm-up starts at the cold interval and converges to the same steady interval.

warmup-with-pacing.title: 7. Warm-up composed with pacing — ramping rate, bounded queue
warmup-with-pacing.note: Composition costs one line: new QueuedLimiter(warmupLimiter, bounds, clock). Both admit at the warm-up rate; the bounded one refuses callers it cannot serve within the bound instead of letting waits grow without limit.

cost-function.title: Cost function — acquisition interval against stored permits (§5.4)
cost-function.note: Flat at the stable interval below the threshold, sloping up to the cold interval at maxPermits.
